clue.text: Community's thus with other people around group of islands

definitions.note: read as 'of a community', an adjective

indicators.note: around says the first pair of pieces is wrapped about the islands

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
et al, Latin for 'and others'
CI is the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A remote island community describes itself as a place where folk live alongside one another.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are British Crown dependencies off the coast of Normandy, and crosswords often abbreviate them.
explanation.definitionFit: Societal is the adjective for society, so it describes what belongs to a community.

clue.text: Admitters of wicked things, namely at one time originally sinful

parts.note: sc. is the abbreviation of scilicet, Latin for namely
once means at one time, formerly

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the next word, sinful, taking just its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of sinful

explanation.surface: Penitents confess their wicked deeds in church, and one was a sinner long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' is not evil here: wicked things are things with wicks, candles, and a sconce is a wall bracket that admits them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sconce is a wall bracket for candles, so it takes in wick-bearing items.

clue.text: Charlie — hurting no one, appealing to no one?

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
harmless means doing no hurt

explanation.surface: A man named Charlie is inoffensive but has no allure for anybody.
explanation.definitionFit: Something charmless lacks any attractive quality, so it pleases nobody.

clue.text: English member is first to thank one expressing mournful thoughts

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

indicators.note: first to points to the opening letter of the word thank that follows

parts.note: first letter of thank

explanation.surface: An English club member is the first to offer thanks to someone grieving.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegist writes elegies, poems of lament for the dead.

clue.text: A second quote's to be given for what medical practitioner will treat

parts.note: read as 'quotes', a verb: to quote is to cite

explanation.surface: A doctor asked for a second opinion is to give another estimate for treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascites is a build-up of fluid in the abdomen, a condition doctors treat.

clue.text: Overnight accommodation reportedly needed for these deliveries

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for these sleeping places is to be taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: berths are sleeping places on a ship or train

explanation.surface: Sleeping quarters are required for the people delivering goods overnight.
explanation.definitionFit: A delivery in obstetrics is a birth, the baby being delivered.

clue.text: David's wife in university city, the woman with arts degree

parts.note: Bath is an English city with a university
she is the pronoun for a woman
BA, Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A wife living in a university town, a woman with a humanities degree.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Bathsheba was married to King David after Uriah's death.

clue.text: What club isn't providing punishment for player?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: clubs are a black suit, so a club is never a card of the red colour
second meaning: the referee's sending-off in football

explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a football club, which ties in with the player, but it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee shows a red card to send a footballer off, a penalty for serious foul play.

clue.text: Nellie is entertained by the fellow who comes from Greece?

definitions.note: read as 'one who comes from Greece', a noun

indicators.note: being entertained by someone means being taken in as a guest, so the name goes inside

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a fellow
Nellie is a pet form of the name Ellen

explanation.surface: A woman called Nellie is hosted by a man who might be Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: Nellie is not taken letter by letter: it stands for the full name it is a nickname of.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hellene is a Greek, from Hellas, the Greeks' own name for their country.

clue.text: Sparkling old friend with energy and fragrance

parts.note: a pal is a friend
E is the physics symbol for energy
a scent is a fragrance

explanation.surface: An old friend arrives full of energy and a lovely perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Opalescent describes the shimmering, iridescent play of colour seen in opal.

clue.text: Model to perform when given lines

parts.note: to do is to perform
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A fashion model is ready to perform once handed a script.
explanation.definitionFit: A doll is a small model of a human figure.

clue.text: Sometime get act sorted out? Bill will go through it

indicators.note: something sorted out has been put into new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a piece of legislation will be dealt with eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is a parliamentary bill.
explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament a bill is examined clause by clause at its committee stage before becoming law.

clue.text: Easiest assignments — only some needed rests

indicators.note: only some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Even with the simplest tasks, a few people still had to take breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Siestas are afternoon naps, rests taken in the heat of the day.

clue.text: A dean's original sermon maybe in worship

indicators.note: original takes the beginning of the word dean's, its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of dean's
a sermon is one kind of oration, a formal speech

explanation.surface: A cathedral dean's first sermon is perhaps part of a service of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is reverent love and praise, as given to God.

clue.text: Bent on being still attached to clique

parts.note: dead means motionless, still
a set is a group of people, a clique

explanation.surface: Someone determined to stay part of an exclusive group.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dead set on something is to be fully determined to have it.

clue.text: Says fish could be heading towards America

parts.note: states means says
the ide is a freshwater fish, also called orfe

explanation.surface: Someone claims a fish might be migrating across the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Stateside is an adverb meaning to or in the United States.

clue.text: Get rid of some French politician, twisted inside

parts.note: des is the French for 'some'

indicators.note: twisted says the politician's letters are turned about, here only the inner pair

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A call to eliminate a French politician who is corrupt at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the inner two letters of TORY swap, giving TROY.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy something is to do away with it completely.

clue.text: Understanding number in part of hospital will require particular drug

indicators.note: in places the number inside the hospital department

parts.note: ENT, the ear, nose and throat department
ten is a number
E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A patient on a ward will need a certain medication.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is an informal understanding between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale.

clue.text: Sympathy for all that trouble with foreign money lost

parts.note: though means nevertheless, for all that

indicators.note: lost says the currency is taken away from trouble

parts.note: the rouble is the Russian currency

explanation.surface: Commiserations for the bother of losing money on exchange abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking ROUBLE out of 'trouble' leaves just T.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought can mean consideration or kindly concern for others, as in 'a thoughtful gesture'.

clue.text: Celebrity entertained by wicked person with sinister sign

indicators.note: being entertained by someone is being taken into their home, so the celebrity goes inside

parts.note: bad means wicked
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A star is hosted by a villain who bears an ominous mark.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry the bar sinister (strictly the bend or baton sinister) on a coat of arms marks illegitimate birth.
explanation.definitionFit: An illegitimate child's arms traditionally carried a sinister band, the mark of illegitimacy.

clue.text: Lawyers met with anger and torrent of abuse?

parts.note: the Bar is the collective body of barristers
rage is anger

explanation.surface: Barristers faced fury and a stream of insults.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage, strictly an artillery bombardment, is also a rapid outpouring of words such as complaints.

clue.text: Man moving into place is one of the old people

indicators.note: into puts the reordered word inside the place

parts.note: a site is a place

indicators.note: moving says the letters of man shift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man relocating to a new spot is one of an ancient tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Samnites were an ancient Italic people of the southern Apennines who fought Rome.

clue.text: Joy of journalist lifted by something illuminating

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means the editor is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
a light is something that illuminates

explanation.surface: A reporter's happiness at being raised up by a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Delight is great pleasure, a synonym of joy.

clue.text: Statesman's howler — most calm in turmoil?

indicators.note: turmoil is confusion, so these letters are thrown into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician's blunder leaves the serenest person in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Cromwell was Henry VIII's chief minister, a leading Tudor politician.

clue.text: Cosy little room where weapons thrown back

indicators.note: thrown back says the word for weapons runs from its end to its start

parts.note: guns are weapons

explanation.surface: A comfortable small room where arms were hurled aside.
explanation.walkthrough: A snug is a small, comfortable private bar in a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: In a British pub the snug is a small cosy side room, often private.

clue.text: Being unrealistic about one bit of business, I celebrate

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a deal is a business transaction
to sing of something is to celebrate it

explanation.surface: Having closed one business deal, I celebrate, though I may be kidding myself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealising something is picturing it as perfect, which is seeing it unrealistically.

clue.text: College with fashionable folk by the sea in Brittany

indicators.note: by means beside, the fashionable folk placed next to the sea

parts.note: mer is French for sea, and Brittany is in France
ton is the fashionable world, high society

explanation.surface: A college term spent with smart society at the French seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: Merton is one of the oldest colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: Son faces tough challenge — more dangerous than any other

parts.note: Everest, the highest mountain, is the byword for a supreme challenge

explanation.surface: A son confronts a tough climb, the riskiest of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Severest is the superlative of severe, which can describe the most perilous or grave conditions.
